successors.name: Commonwealth of Australia
successors.text: 'Australian mandate commencing 17 December 1920' over Kaiser-Wilhelmsland, the Bismarck Archipelago and the North Solomons: the part of Papua New Guinea outside Papua

successors.name: South Seas Mandate
successors.text: the Caroline Islands, Palau, the Mariana Islands (except Guam) and the Marshall Islands: 'The islands north of the equator became the Japanese League of Nations Mandate for the South Seas Islands'

successors.name: Territory of Nauru
successors.text: Nauru: Australian troops 'held control until 1920', then the League of Nations mandate (History of Nauru)

ledger.x: 1884: the German flag is raised over northeast New Guinea and the Bismarck Archipelago (3 November 1884).
1885: the North Solomon Islands (Bougainville and Buka) become a German protectorate: 'the North Solomon Islands were declared a German protectorate in 1885'.
1891: the seat moves from Finschhafen to Friedrich-Wilhelmshafen (infobox 1891-1899).
1899: the seat moves to Herbertshöhe (Kokopo), infobox 1899-1910.
1899: Germany buys the Caroline Islands, Palau and the Marianas from Spain: 'The Caroline Islands, Palau, and the Mariana Islands (except for Guam) were bought from Spain in 1899.'
1899: direct imperial control replaces the New Guinea Company: infobox 'Direct control established: 12 February 1899'.

1906: the Marshall Islands (and Nauru) are annexed to German New Guinea: 'The Marshall Islands, which had been a German protectorate since 1885, were annexed to German New Guinea in 1906'; the protectorate 'also included Nauru'.
1910: the seat moves to Simpsonhafen (Rabaul), infobox 1910-1914.

1914: Australia captures Nauru: after the outbreak of the First World War the island 'was captured by Australian troops' (History of Nauru; the Nauru page: 'captured and occupied by Australian troops').
1914: Japan occupies German Micronesia: infobox 'Japanese occupation: 29 September 1914'; 'Japan occupied most of the remaining German possessions in the Pacific.'
1920: the Australian military control of Nauru ends: Australian troops 'held control until 1920' (History of Nauru); the mandate itself is dated 1923 on the pages (terms drawn up in 1920).

1920: Nauru passes to the Australian mandate: 'The terms of the League of Nations mandate were drawn up in 1920' (Nauru), conferred on Australia in 1923 with the United Kingdom and New Zealand as co-trustees (History of Nauru).
1920: the Australian military occupation of New Guinea ends as the mandate begins (17 December 1920).

1920: the Japanese occupation of Micronesia gives way to the League of Nations mandate for the South Seas Islands: 'The islands north of the equator became the Japanese League of Nations Mandate for the South Seas Islands.'
1920: German Micronesia passes to Japan as the South Seas Mandate: 'The islands north of the equator became the Japanese League of Nations Mandate for the South Seas Islands.'

wars.name: Australian occupation of German New Guinea (First World War)
wars.outcome: The Australian Naval and Military Expeditionary Force attacked Bita Paka; 'On 21 September all German forces in the colony surrendered'; the colony stayed under Australian occupation to the mandate of 17 December 1920.

wars.name: Japanese occupation of German Micronesia (First World War)
wars.outcome: 'Japan occupied most of the remaining German possessions in the Pacific' (infobox 'Japanese occupation: 29 September 1914'); they became the South Seas Mandate.
